subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: Which durable trust and influence fields must every memory plugin support once source provenance is available?
rationale: Source transport and lineage can be implemented mechanically, but deciding whether unreviewed content may be retained, recalled, or influence planning—and how trusted operators override defaults—requires explicit security and product intent.

options.title: Minimal shared trust contract
options.body: Standardize causal source, review state, and influence eligibility across memory plugins while leaving expiration and ranking parameters plugin-owned.

options.title: Default-plugin policy only
options.body: Implement trust controls only in the recommended memory plugin without expanding the public memory contract.

options.title: External policy integrations
options.body: Keep OpenClaw limited to provenance plumbing and leave the full trust model to external memory or MCP integrations.

recommendation.title: Minimal shared trust contract
recommendation.body: Standardize causal source, review state, and influence eligibility across memory plugins while leaving expiration and ranking parameters plugin-owned.

likelyOwner.reason: Current memory-contract and canonical provenance history make this the strongest available owner for the shared schema and plugin-boundary decision.
